rv.q: That’s a high quality group, and The Counter fits right in.
Happily, the playwright has an ideal partner in Mr. Cromer, whose flair for mining emotional depth through intimacy has helped make him one of theater’s most sought-out directors.
How this happens in “The Counter” is not entirely predictable, but neither is it terribly convincing.

cn.t: Kennedy's diner drama about two lonely souls forging an unlikely friendship features strong performances from Edwards and Flood, but critics find the play itself uneven—some praise its intriguing character work while others call it shaggy and predictable.

vr.q: The whole production had this very genuine bittersweet quality that really worked for me.
